summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, diabetes, morbid obesity, and a history of recurrent infections and thromboses was admitted after spontaneous bleeding from a recent right groin abscess during dialysis. She was found to have an arteriovenous fistula involving the right common femoral and profunda arteries, requiring surgical repair with significant blood loss. Postoperatively, she developed a wound infection with Klebsiella pneumoniae and Proteus mirabilis, necessitating a change to IV meropenem. A wound VAC was placed, and a PICC line was inserted for antibiotic administration. She remained hemodynamically stable, resumed dialysis, and was transitioned to extended care with a plan for continued wound management, IV antibiotics, and follow-up. Her warfarin was restarted, and medications were adjusted for her comorbidities.
